parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime shows no documented traveler-facing restriction: no criminalisation, no facility rules, no entry screening (open border), and foreign documents govern throughout the stay. Documented social acceptance is real (2019 referendum, openly gay head of state, inclusive curriculum). The gaps are on the protection side: hate-crime enhancements, constitutional non-discrimination, and sentence enhancements cover sexual orientation only, gender identity has no statutory footing despite accepted 2019 UPR recommendations, and anti-LGBTQ violence is occasional with no published figures. That is a thin-recourse gap, not an active exposure, so it holds the score below the fully-protected tier.

entry_documents.exposure: None documented. No identity screening at the open land border or entry; a visitor's foreign documents govern identity throughout the stay.
entry_documents.protection: Documented absence of friction: entry carries no documented friction and no screening that would out an arriving trans visitor.
entry_documents.interaction: Border stage completes cleanly; document mismatches never arise because local reissuance does not touch visitors.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No statute regulates gender identity or presentation; no arrests, custody placement rules, or police practice targeting trans people are recorded.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Decriminalisation since 1864; residual Article 274 repealed in 2004 and never reported as applied.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No custody pathway documented for visitors; hate-crime enhancements do not cover gender identity if an incident reaches police.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No statute regulates which bathrooms or facilities a person may use; no subnational variation recorded.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Documented absence of facility restriction; unitary system with no regional divergence.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility use is unregulated at all levels, so a family with a minor faces no state-imposed placement rule.

care_services.exposure: Not documented for visitors. No recorded denial of care; civil unions carry healthcare rights but marriage/household gaps are resident-facing.
care_services.protection: Civil-union healthcare rights exist; inclusive sex/citizenship education signals institutional culture.
care_services.interaction: Visitor's own insurance/home-country documents govern any care episode; no local exclusion recorded.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Gender identity absent from the 2008 hate-crime provision, constitutional Article 4 (2019 referendum), and 2019 UPR acceptance with no implementing text — a thin-recourse gap, not active hostility.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Documented official friendliness: openly gay head of state (2022), 71.46% referendum, accepted UPR gender-identity recommendations.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: If an assault occurs, sentence enhancements would not apply on gender-identity grounds; police framing is undocumented either way.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No facility, custody, or entry rule that would treat a travelling minor or accompanying parent differently on gender-identity grounds.
minors_guardians.protection: Inclusive citizenship and sex education curricula indicate an institutional culture tolerant of gender diversity.
minors_guardians.interaction: School-age exposure is limited to a short visit; no documented registration or screening rule applies.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Occasional violence against LGBTQ people is reported, without published figures permitting comparison to the general crime rate — no pattern, count, or state-tolerance documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime enhancements exist for sexual orientation (application undocumented); no trans-specific targeting recorded.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Whether police respond protectively to a trans victim is not documented; enhancements would not attach on gender identity.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Gender identity lacks statutory footing in hate-crime, constitutional, and non-discrimination layers; no enforcement data on the 2008 enhancements.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Working civil society and institutions are implied by referendum process, UPR engagement, and documented legislative debate.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: A visitor's practical recourse for a gender-identity-motivated incident is an open question, not a documented denial.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: Vellandra has a routine, universal entry bar with near-nil appeal. Here entry is frictionless, the border is open, and foreign documents govern. No register, no exclusion, no enforced discretion against trans visitors exists in the record.

Higher than 0.55-B: Kestrel Isles shows discretionary secondary screening with inconsistent refusal of entry. This dossier documents the opposite at the border — no screening at all — and no administrative penalty pathway. Its residual weaknesses are protection gaps, not active border exposures.

Modestly higher than 0.75-C: Meridia accepts markers matching presentation but retains secondary-screening discretion and unclear guidance. This jurisdiction has no documented friction whatsoever, but also lacks gender-identity coverage in its protective machinery, which keeps it out of the 0.85+ tier.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is consistently permissive at every journey stage: open border, foreign documents authoritative, no facility or conduct statute, decriminalised status, and a documented tolerant climate (2019 referendum, openly gay head of state, inclusive curricula). The documented weakness is asymmetric protection — every legal safeguard (hate-crime enhancements, constitutional clause, sentence uplifts) covers sexual orientation only, and accepted UPR gender-identity recommendations have no implementing text. That is a recourse gap for an outed traveller facing the occasional, undated anti-LGBTQ violence the dossier reports, not a state-imposed exposure. No tier-1 or tier-2 feature appears: no facility rule, no custody placement by birth sex, no police targeting. Absence of enforcement data is uncertainty, and thin data here sits atop decriminalisation plus documented acceptance, so it resolves high but below the fully-protected tier.
